idiom_name: SwiftNIO Channel + ByteBuffer framing, or distributed actors for generated remote calls
implementation_notes: The roles are assembled from SwiftNIO primitives: a ClientBootstrap/ServerBootstrap creates a Channel, ByteBuffer (with writeInteger/getInteger for the length header) or a length-field frame decoder performs the framing, and a ChannelHandler - or the async NIOAsyncChannel wrapper - receives whole frames and dispatches to the peer, so the receiver loop and the marshalling boundary both live inside the pipeline. Apple's distributed-actor runtime is the other end of the spectrum: a `distributed actor` plus a DistributedActorSystem turns a call on a remote actor reference into exactly the marshal-send-unmarshal-dispatch sequence this pattern prescribes, with Codable as the codec and the remote reference as the forwarder. Hand-written roles remain justified when the peer must interoperate with a non-Swift or non-NIO counterpart.
pitfalls: Reading moves the ByteBuffer reader index: peek with getInteger(at:) or mark/restore, otherwise a half-read frame is lost - the classic SwiftNIO framing bug.
ChannelHandler state may only be mutated on the channel's event loop, and blocking that loop stalls every channel in the group.
A borrowed ByteBuffer slice must not outlive its buffer, and a distributed-actor call still needs an explicit policy for an unreachable remote actor.
